part.text:
I've confirmed the structural facts. Here is my read-only quality review of `workspace.dsl` as a C4 model.

## Findings

- **System context view `GuestContext` is built on missing system-level relationships.** Every relationship in the model is defined at the *container* level (`guest -> portal`, `guest -> mobile`, `deposits -> payments`, `concierge -> loyaltyFeed`). A C4 system-context diagram shows the people and external systems interacting with the *system as a whole*, and a Structurizr `systemContext` view renders the system plus the elements that have a direct relationship with it. Because the guest, `payments`, `loyaltyFeed`, and `legacy` have no relationship to `planner` itself, none of them will appear in `GuestContext` — the view that claims to "show the guest's journey around the system" will render the system in isolation. System-level edges (e.g. `guest -> planner "Books and manages stays" "HTTPS"`) are absent.

- **`legacy` (Legacy Booking System) is an orphan with a self-contradictory description.** It has no relationships at all, and its description says both "retired" and "being phased out." If it is truly retired it does not belong in the model; if it is being phased out, the model should show the migration/coexistence relationship. As written it is dead weight that misleads the reader.

- **`tariff` (Tariff Rules Library) is a library mis-modeled as a container.** A C4 container is a deployable unit; a rules library is not. The `rate -> tariff` relationship is labeled "in-process," which confirms it is not a separate deployment. It should be a *component* of the `rate` service (C4 level 3), not a peer container at level 2. This misrepresents the deployment topology.

- **`payments` (Payment Gateway) uses the generic `element` type and is not marked external.** A third-party payment gateway is an external system and should be a `softwareSystem` tagged `External`. The generic `element` type discards C4 semantics, and the missing `External` tag makes it look like an internal part of the system.

- **`loyaltyFeed` (Loyalty Points Feed) uses the generic `element` type.** It carries an `External` tag, but the type should still be `softwareSystem` to correctly represent an external system in C4.

- **The mobile app client is missing.** `mobile` is the "Mobile App Backend," whose description says it "serves the hotel group's mobile app" — yet the app the guest actually uses is not modeled. The guest is shown talking straight to the backend (`guest -> mobile "Books rooms via" "HTTPS"`), which is not how it works. The mobile app should be its own container with the guest using it.

- **`portal -> rate` has a vacuous description: "uses."** C4 relationships should carry a meaningful verb phrase stating the purpose (e.g. "calculates rates for" / "requests pricing from"). "uses" conveys nothing.

- **Six containers have no incoming relationships and are therefore unreachable:** `housekeeping`, `concierge`, `deposits`, `feedback`, `reporting`, and `availability`. Nothing in the model triggers or calls them, so it is unclear how they participate in the system. Expected edges are missing — e.g. `portal`/`mobile -> availability` (room search), `portal`/`stays -> deposits` (charging a deposit on booking), `scheduler -> reporting` (nightly reports), `portal`/`mobile -> feedback` and `-> concierge` (guest requests).

- **`scheduler` (Batch Scheduler) is a dead end.** It receives "Registers nightly tasks in" from `stays` but has no outgoing relationships to the jobs it runs. The model never shows what the scheduler actually triggers (e.g. `reporting`), so its purpose is unexplained.

- **Database descriptions are inconsistent with the relationships drawn.** `staydb` is described as storing "stay, room, occupancy, and task records," but the `stays` and `rooms` services that would write stay and room records have no edge to it (only `housekeeping` writes, and `availability`/`reporting` read). Likewise `guestdb` stores "guest and deposit records" yet no service writes guest records, and `mediadb` stores "contracts, invoices, and guest media" yet no service writes contracts or invoices. The descriptions promise data flows the model does not show.

- **The `container planner` view has no description.** The `systemContext` view is described, but the container view is not. Minor, but C4 practice is to give every view a one-line purpose.

The model is otherwise well-formed: the person, the in-scope system, the container set, and the two C4 levels (context + container) are all present, and most element and relationship descriptions are clear and specific. The issues above are the ones that break C4 conventions or leave the model incomplete/inconsistent.
